container_info.description:
Create a clear, non-technical document for a BMI (Body Mass Index) Calculator, including what it does, how to use it, required inputs (height and weight), calculation formula, BMI category ranges, assumptions/validation, and example calculations. Intended for end users and basic implementation reference.

Document Type: document
Title: BMI Calculator – Documentation
Outline:
1. Overview
2. What is BMI?
3. Inputs Required
4. How the BMI Calculator Works (Formula)
5. BMI Categories (Ranges)
6. How to Use (Step-by-step)
7. Examples
8. Validation & Edge Cases
9. Disclaimer
10. FAQ
container_info.reasoning: The deliverable is a non-technical user-facing document (documentation) for a BMI Calculator rather than an interactive application or API. The container already includes documentation tooling such as mkdocs and sphinx. MkDocs is a lightweight, headless-friendly static documentation generator (Markdown-based) well suited for producing the requested structured document and example pages. Classifying the platform as 'utility' fits documentation generation rather than web/mobile/backend. MkDocs is minimal, works in a headless container, and produces static site output that can be served if needed.
requirements: markdown files (project/docs/*.md) following the provided outline
mkdocs.yml site configuration with site_name and nav entries matching the outline
a basic theme (mkdocs default) — no extra plugins required
headless build command: mkdocs build (outputs site/ directory)
optional local preview: mkdocs serve (for local testing; not required for headless build)

steps.name: Environment verification and safe mkdocs install
steps.description: Verify python3, pip and git are available. Detect preinstalled mkdocs and report its version. If mkdocs is missing or a configurable MIN_MK_VERSION is set and the preinstalled mkdocs is older, install/upgrade mkdocs into the user's Python site (--user). Persist a single /etc/profile.d file idempotently only if a --user install was performed and the user bin directory is not already available to future shells. Use a pure-Python version comparator to avoid relying on pkg_resources. Operates in workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS_DEFAULT="/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation"
WS="${WORKSPACE:-$WS_DEFAULT}"
PY=python3
PIP="$PY -m pip"
MIN_MK_VERSION=""  # optionally set to e.g. "1.4.2"
command -v "$PY" >/dev/null || { echo "python3 not found" >&2; exit 2; }
$PY -m pip --version >/dev/null || { echo "pip (python3 -m pip) not available" >&2; exit 3; }
# pure-Python comparator: exit 0 if v1 >= v2, non-zero otherwise
ver_ge() { $PY - <<'PY'
import sys
A=sys.argv[1].split('.') if len(sys.argv)>1 else ['0']
B=sys.argv[2].split('.') if len(sys.argv)>2 else ['0']
A=[int(x) if x.isdigit() else x for x in A]
B=[int(x) if x.isdigit() else x for x in B]
for a,b in zip(A, B):
    if a> b:
        sys.exit(0)
    if a< b:
        sys.exit(1)
if len(A)>=len(B):
    sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)
PY
}
# check existing mkdocs
if command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  prever=$(mkdocs --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' || true)
  echo "preinstalled mkdocs: ${prever:-unknown}"
  INSTALL_USER=0
  if [ -n "$MIN_MK_VERSION" ]; then
    if [ -z "$prever" ]; then
      INSTALL_USER=1
    else
      if ! ver_ge "$prever" "$MIN_MK_VERSION"; then
        INSTALL_USER=1
      fi
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "mkdocs not found on PATH"
  INSTALL_USER=1
fi
# attempt pip --user install/upgrade if requested
if [ "${INSTALL_USER:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then
  # retry small number of times for transient network errors
  set +e
  n=0; rc=1
  until [ $n -ge 3 ] || [ $rc -eq 0 ]; do
    $PIP install --user --upgrade mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; n=$((n+1)); sleep 1
  done
  set -e
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "pip --user install mkdocs failed" >&2; exit 4; fi
  # ensure user base bin is available now and persisted idempotently
  PIP_USER_BASE=$($PY -m site --user-base 2>/dev/null || true)
  USER_BIN="${PIP_USER_BASE%/}/bin"
  if [ -d "$USER_BIN" ]; then
    export PATH="$USER_BIN:$PATH"
    PROFILE_FILE="/etc/profile.d/mkdocs-userbin.sh"
    if [ ! -f "$PROFILE_FILE" ]; then
      echo "export PATH=\"${USER_BIN}:\$PATH\"" | sudo tee "$PROFILE_FILE" >/dev/null
      sudo chmod 0755 "$PROFILE_FILE"
    fi
  fi
fi
# final validation
command -v mkdocs >/dev/null || { echo "mkdocs not found on PATH after install" >&2; exit 5; }
echo "mkdocs: $(mkdocs --version)"
$PY -m pip show mkdocs 2>/dev/null || true
exit 0

steps.summary: Verified python3, pip and git availability; detect existing mkdocs and its version; perform a user-level pip install/upgrade of mkdocs only if needed (missing or older than MIN_MK_VERSION). If a --user install is performed and the user's pip bin directory is not already guaranteed to be on PATH for future shells, the script writes a single idempotent /etc/profile.d/mkdocs-userbin.sh to export the user bin into PATH. steps.name: Project scaffolding and mkdocs site files
steps.description: Create docs/*.md and mkdocs.yml in the workspace following the required outline. Use MkDocs default theme by omitting an explicit theme block (keeps headless build simple). Do not pre-create site/ (mkdocs will produce it). Create concise build and serve wrappers that cd into the workspace so they work from any CWD. Initialize git repo idempotently; attempt an initial commit only if git user.name and user.email are configured. Create .gitignore to exclude site/ and Python artifacts and add a README. Operates in workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS_DEFAULT="/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation"
WS="${WORKSPACE:-$WS_DEFAULT}"
mkdir -p "$WS" && cd "$WS"
mkdir -p docs
cat > docs/index.md <<'MD'
# BMI Calculator Documentation

Welcome to the BMI Calculator documentation.

MD
cat > docs/usage.md <<'MD'
# Usage

How to use the BMI calculator.

MD
cat > docs/installation.md <<'MD'
# Installation

Installation instructions for the BMI calculator.

MD
cat > docs/api.md <<'MD'
# API

API reference for the BMI calculator (if applicable).

MD
# mkdocs.yml using default bundled theme (omit theme block to use default)
cat > mkdocs.yml <<'YML'
site_name: BMI Calculator Documentation
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Usage: usage.md
  - Installation: installation.md
  - API: api.md
YML
# .gitignore and README
cat > .gitignore <<'G'
site/
*.pyc
__pycache__/
G
cat > README.md <<'R'
Simple MkDocs site. Use ./build.sh to build and ./serve.sh to preview locally.
MkDocs is preinstalled in the container image when available.
R
# helper wrapper scripts
cat > build.sh <<B
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="${WS}"
cd "$WS"
mkdocs build --clean
B
chmod +x build.sh
cat > serve.sh <<S
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="${WS}"
cd "$WS"
mkdocs serve --dev-addr=127.0.0.1:8000
S
chmod +x serve.sh
# initialize git repo if absent
if [ ! -d .git ]; then
  git init -q || true
fi
if git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if git config --get user.name >/dev/null && git config --get user.email >/dev/null; then
    git add -A >/dev/null || true
    git commit -m "scaffold mkdocs site" >/dev/null || true
  else
    echo "git user.name/user.email not set; skipping initial commit" >&2
  fi
fi
exit 0

output_scripts.name: install
output_scripts.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS_DEFAULT="/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation"
WS="${WORKSPACE:-$WS_DEFAULT}"
# verify essentials
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "python3 not found" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v pip3 >/dev/null || { echo "pip3 not found" >&2; exit 3; }
command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "git not found" >&2; exit 4; }
# check mkdocs; do not reinstall if present
MK_ON_PATH=$(command -v mkdocs || true)
if [ -n "$MK_ON_PATH" ]; then
  mkdocs --version || true
  exit 0
fi
# mkdocs not found on PATH; check pip-installed package availability
PYMKVERS=""
if python3 -c "import mkdocs, sys; print(getattr(mkdocs,'__version__',''))" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c "import mkdocs; print(mkdocs.__version__)"
  exit 0
fi
# If we reach here, mkdocs module not available; attempt user install
pip3 install --user --upgrade mkdocs >/dev/null
# ensure user base bin is on PATH for future shells via /etc/profile.d if needed
USER_BASE=$(python3 -c "import site; print(site.getuserbase())")
USER_BIN="$USER_BASE/bin"
if ! echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -xq "$USER_BIN"; then
  if [ -w /etc/profile.d ]; then
    cat >/etc/profile.d/mkdocs_user_path.sh <<EOF
# added by scaffold install to expose pip user installs
export PATH="$USER_BIN:":"$PATH"
EOF
    chmod 0644 /etc/profile.d/mkdocs_user_path.sh || true
  fi
fi
# final check
if ! command -v mkdocs >/dev/null; then
  echo "mkdocs installed to user site; mkdocs not on PATH in this session." >&2
  echo "You may need to relogin or run: export PATH=\"$USER_BIN:\$PATH\"" >&2
  exit 0
fi
mkdocs --version

steps.description: Run mkdocs build (headless) to generate the static site into site/ and verify site/index.html contains the site title. Fail fast if mkdocs is not on PATH. #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS_DEFAULT="/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation"

steps.name: Validation: build, serve, smoke-test and clean shutdown
steps.description: Validate: run mkdocs build, start mkdocs serve in its own session, wait up to ~20s with backoff for it to serve, curl the site to confirm content, then cleanly stop the server with TERM then KILL escalation. Avoid unnecessary sudo when killing processes started by the same user. Provide diagnostics (serve log) on failure. Operates in workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS_DEFAULT="/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/bmi-calculator--documentation-236912-236913/Documentation"
WS="${WORKSPACE:-$WS_DEFAULT}"
cd "$WS"
command -v mkdocs >/dev/null || { echo "mkdocs not found on PATH; run env-001" >&2; exit 2; }
LOG=/tmp/mkdocs.serve.$$; rm -f "$LOG" || true
mkdocs build --clean >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "mkdocs build failed" >&2; exit 6; }
# start serve in its own session, capture PID
setsid mkdocs serve --dev-addr=127.0.0.1:8000 >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
# derive PGID; fallback to PID if ps fails
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
# wait sequence summing ~20s: 1+2+4+8+5
OK=0
for s in 1 2 4 8 5; do
  sleep $s
  if curl -sSf "http://127.0.0.1:8000/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then OK=1; break; fi
done
if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "mkdocs serve did not start in time; last 200 lines of log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  # attempt graceful shutdown (no sudo unless required)
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; else kill -TERM "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
  sleep 2
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; else kill -KILL "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
  exit 7
fi
# verify served content
if ! curl -sSf "http://127.0.0.1:8000/" | grep -q "BMI Calculator Documentation"; then
  echo "served content unexpected; tail of log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; else kill -TERM "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
  sleep 1
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; else kill -KILL "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
  exit 8
fi
# stop server cleanly: TERM, wait, then KILL if needed
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; else kill -TERM "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
sleep 2
# escalate if still running
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
  if ps -o pid= -g "$PGID" | grep -q .; then kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
else
  if ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then kill -KILL "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
  pkill -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
sleep 1 || true
[ -d site ] || { echo "site directory missing after build" >&2; exit 9; }
echo "built: $WS/site/index.html"
rm -f "$LOG" || true
exit 0
